entries.justification: 4/16 workloads return host-capacity CUDA OOM (12/16 PASS): the largest-shape attention-softmax-dropout-value BACKWARD materializes [batch, num_heads=80, seq_q, seq_kv] fp32 score-grad intermediates that exceed the RTX 3090 Ti's 24 GiB. Two phases observed: INVALID_REFERENCE 'Reference run() failed: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 5.10 GiB' (batch=32, seq_q=691, seq_kv=773) and RUNTIME_ERROR 'Timing failed: CUDA out of memory' (batch=4, seq_q=1024, seq_kv=2048, 1.25 GiB; batch=32, 512x512, 2.50 GiB). All four are CUDA-OOM strings (host memory capacity), NOT INCORRECT_NUMERICAL and NOT an sm_86 compile/portability defect; expected to fit on B200 (192 GB). In-scope (NOT an AC-1 exclusion); deferred only on the 24 GiB host.

workload (batch_size=2, seq_len=8192) returns sol-execbench INVALID_REFERENCE: 'Reference run() failed: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 16.00 GiB' — the full decoder-layer attention materializes a 16 GiB [B,heads,S,S] fp32 tensor in the reference run() at the largest shape, exceeding the RTX 3090 Ti's 24 GiB. 17/18 PASS. Local-host memory-capacity limit on the reference (not a kernel/sm_86 numerical or compile defect); expected to fit on B200 (192 GB). In-scope (NOT an AC-1 exclusion); deferred only on the 24 GiB host.

9/18 workloads return sol-execbench RUNTIME_ERROR 'Timing failed: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 416.00 MiB ... 23.13 GiB already in use' — the H=16384,I=53248 SwiGLU-MLP-backward working set (weights + the reference's fp32 [B,S,I] temporaries, ~the operator-noted ~28 GiB) leaves the 24 GiB host with no headroom for the timing-phase allocation, even under the minimal-timing config. 9/18 PASS. Local-host memory-capacity limit (not a kernel/sm_86 numerical or compile defect); expected to fit on B200 (192 GB). In-scope (NOT an AC-1 exclusion); deferred only on the 24 GiB host.
